cw_sweepstakes_14028: The ARRL Sweepstakes contest. The strongest signal decodes as a complete contest exchange: K0SN (Montana) sends W4IX serial 349, class U, licensed 75, section MT, then TU. Weaker CW signals are visible at 1170, 2000 and 2340 Hz but were below what the decoder copies cleanly.
psk31_14070: One weak, narrow signal at 1377 Hz, coming and going. Too weak to decode: the PSK31 decoder copies a synthetic test message exactly, so the signal, not the decoder, is the limit.
js8_14078: One weak signal near 1727 Hz. Decoded offline with the radio's own JS8 receiver (tools/js8_play, all four speeds): nothing. The same player decodes a synthetic two-station JS8 band exactly, so the signal was too weak or not JS8.
ft4_14080: FT4 (FT8's faster cousin, 7.5 s slots): one decode, a station in central Chile calling CQ.
rtty_14083: No RTTY signal in this 30 s window. The RTTY decoder copies a synthetic test signal correctly.
ssb_voice_14305: No voice found. The 'loudest' spot on 14.150-14.350 was a steady comb of tones 60 Hz apart (the horizontal lines at 600-1050 Hz): electrical interference, most likely from something near the antenna, not a station.
sstv_14230: No SSTV picture was being sent during these 60 s; the band is noise only.
chu_14670: CHU (Ottawa) not heard: the S-meter sat at its floor and the audio is noise.
wwv_15000: WWV/WWVH not heard: noise only. 15 MHz is outside the 20 m coil setting and usually fades after dark.
broadcast_15770: A shortwave broadcast station (15.770 MHz is one of WRMI's frequencies, Okeechobee, Florida). Weak, but programme audio is there: the curved stripes in the first 12 s are voice or singing. Listen to the recording.
wspr_14095_6: One full 2-minute WSPR cycle (01:10 UTC) through the repo's own wsprd: no spots, and no WSPR traces are visible in the 1400-1600 Hz window either.
ncdxf_beacons_14100: Cut short at 60 s: the radio rebooted onto the test kernel at 01:13 UTC. Of the six beacon slots that were recorded (4U1UN New York through VK6RBP Australia), none stands above the noise.
js8_14078_b: A second try after the radio came back (three slots, 01:22:30-01:23:16 UTC): the band is noise only here, no JS8 transmissions at all, so nothing to decode.
ncdxf_beacons_14100_b: The full 3-minute beacon cycle, recorded after the radio came back (01:24 UTC). None of the 18 beacons stands above the noise: 20 m had mostly closed by then.
cw_14023_9: The strongest signal in the spectrum (14.0239 MHz, +26 dB at its peak). It was only on in bursts while recorded, and nothing copied cleanly.
cw_14040_cluster: Tuned from the spectrum: two Sweepstakes stations calling CQ, N6RO (California) at 14.0408 and N6AR at 14.0421, plus part of an exchange to N0AX.
cw_14045_cluster: Tuned from the spectrum: a noisy copy, but KL7SB in Alaska comes through, with its exchange's '76 AK' and 'TU KL7SB'.
cw_14056_cluster: Tuned from the spectrum: W6EU sending its exchange, class B, licensed '58, section SV (Sacramento Valley), with 'TU' before it.
carrier_14117_7: One of the steady lines in the spectrum: nothing keyed or modulated on it, so a carrier or local interference, not a station.
cw40_7029_5: Tuned from the spectrum to the strongest CW (7.0302). Sweepstakes at 46 WPM, a noisy copy: K5KU calling (SS K5KU) and a 'TU' comes through.
cw40_7040: The CW group at 7.040-7.043: W6PH calling CQ SS twice, and part of an exchange from WA6KHK (serial 508, class B).
lsb40_7224_5: The strongest voice in the spectrum (7.2202), tuned from the zoomed spectrum to 7.2245 LSB: a voice QSO, clear speech.
lsb40_7251_0: Voice at 7.2501 recorded in LSB: speech, but with a steady 1 kHz whistle, a carrier at 7.250: this is an AM signal. The AM recording below is the right way to hear it.
lsb40_7266_0: Voice at 7.2651 in LSB: speech with the same 1 kHz whistle, an AM signal (carrier 7.265). See the AM recording below.
lsb40_7160_0: Voice at 7.1600, tuned from the zoomed spectrum to 7.160 LSB.
am40_7250: The 7.250 voice in AM, as it is sent: no whistle.
bc40_7505: The strongest broadcaster on the sweep, 7.505 MHz (WRNO, New Orleans, uses this frequency): clear speech and music.
bc40_7355: 41 m broadcast, 7.355 MHz: weaker, programme audio under the noise.
bc40_7490: 41 m broadcast, 7.490 MHz (a frequency WBCQ uses).
bc40_7570: 41 m broadcast, 7.570 MHz (a frequency WRMI uses).
chu_7850: CHU (Ottawa) not heard: noise only, and nothing showed at 7.850 in the spectrum.
psk31_7070: PSK31 window: the decoder's output was noise letters only, no real copy (it decodes a test signal exactly).
rtty_7089: The digital group at 7.0906-7.098: not RTTY that decodes; the output was noise letters only.
ft4_7047_5: FT4: KM6TAU and KQ4CRY finishing a contact (R-10, then R-14).
js8_7078: JS8, decoded offline with the radio's own JS8 receiver (tools/js8_play): W6CJ and K1KFX asking each other 'HW CPY?', and KF5NRU's heartbeat to W6CJ, at normal and turbo speeds.
wspr_7038_6: One 2-minute WSPR cycle (02:50 UTC) through the repo's wsprd: six stations, from Arizona to Oregon, including WW0WWV (the WWV amateur radio club, Colorado).
